excerpt.rendered: A technical overview of Kerberos, ticket-based authentication, and its role in securing network access.

content.rendered:
Kerberos is a network authentication protocol built around trusted ticket exchange rather than repeatedly transmitting user passwords. It is widely used in enterprise environments to authenticate users and services across untrusted networks.

This BitcoinVersus technical note introduces the ticket-granting workflow, the role of the Key Distribution Center, and the operational concepts technicians should understand when troubleshooting authentication failures.

title.rendered: How Bitcoin Mining Efficiency Changes Daily Electricity Costs

excerpt.rendered: How joules per terahash translate into daily power demand and operating cost for Bitcoin miners.

content.rendered:
Mining efficiency directly changes how much electrical power is required to produce a given amount of hashrate. Lower joules per terahash reduce the energy required for the same computational output.

The relationship lets operators compare machine generations, estimate daily electricity consumption, and understand how efficiency improvements change site economics.

title.rendered: Relative Price Explained Through the Power Efficiency Index

content.rendered:
Relative price compares market price with the valuation produced by the Power Efficiency Index. The model evaluates proof-of-work systems through changes in computational capability and energy efficiency.

A market price below the model reading indicates model-relative undervaluation, while a market price above it indicates model-relative overvaluation.

Comparing the models clarifies their assumptions, inputs, and the kinds of market behavior each framework attempts to interpret.

excerpt.rendered: The Power Efficiency Index compares computational performance and energy efficiency with the market price of a proof-of-work asset.

content.rendered:
The Power Efficiency Index (PEI) is a mathematical valuation model within Power Efficiency Theory that compares changes in computational performance and energy efficiency with the market price of a proof-of-work asset.

PEI measures growth in a network’s rate of compute alongside improvements in the energy required per unit of computation. Prices below the PEI estimate suggest undervaluation relative to the model, while prices above it suggest overvaluation.
